authors: Jongha Kim; Byungoh Ko; Jeehye Na; Jinsung Yoon; Hyunwoo J. Kim
why_relevant: Proposes a contrastive decoding method that weights retrieved contexts by relevance to suppress irrelevant/distracting contexts in multimodal RAG, directly addressing robustness to noisy retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on VQA/LVLM setting; not a general text RAG robustness study.

title: RARE: Redundancy-Aware Retrieval Evaluation Framework for High-Similarity Corpora
authors: Hanjun Cho; Jay-Yoon Lee
why_relevant: Introduces a redundancy-aware RAG retrieval evaluation framework and benchmark (RedQA) exposing robustness gaps in retrievers on enterprise corpora with high inter-document similarity.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on evaluation methodology for redundancy rather than directly on noise/conflict/adversarial robustness.

title: Prompt Control-Flow Integrity: A Priority-Aware Runtime Defense Against Prompt Injection in LLM Systems
authors: Md Takrim Ul Alam; Akif Islam; Mohd Ruhul Ameen; Abu Saleh Musa Miah; Jungpil Shin
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: defenses against indirect prompt injection
why_relevant: Proposes a runtime middleware defense against prompt injection attacks, including indirect injection via RAG retrieved documents, enforcing priority among system/developer/user/retrieved segments.
why_not_or_caveat: Evaluated on a small custom synthetic benchmark; defense is generic to LLM APIs rather than RAG-specific, and claims (100% interception, 0% FPR) are limited in scope.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Resolution of Recommendation Conflicts in Multimorbidity Clinical Guidelines
authors: Shiyao Xie; Jian Du
why_relevant: Addresses inter-document knowledge conflicts in retrieved clinical guidelines, proposing a neuro-symbolic SAT-based pipeline to detect retrieved-vs-retrieved conflicts before RAG, and provides a benchmark for guideline conflict detection.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (clinical guidelines) and focuses on knowledge base curation rather than RAG inference robustness directly.

title: MedRAGChecker: Claim-Level Verification for Biomedical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Yuelyu Ji; Min Gu Kwak; Hang Zhang; Xizhi Wu; Chenyu Li; Yanshan Wang
suggested_section: Evaluation and Metrics for RAG Faithfulness
why_relevant: Proposes claim-level verification framework for biomedical RAG that diagnoses faithfulness, under-evidence, contradiction, and safety-critical errors, helping disentangle retrieval vs generation failures.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (biomedical); primarily a verification/evaluation tool rather than a robustness method.

title: Led to Mislead: Adversarial Content Injection for Attacks on Neural Ranking Models
authors: Amin Bigdeli; Amir Khosrojerdi; Radin Hamidi Rad; Morteza Zihayat; Charles L. A. Clarke; Ebrahim Bagheri
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box adversarial attack on neural ranking models via LLM-generated content injection, relevant to retrieval-stage adversarial threats that underlie RAG robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Targets ranking manipulation rather than RAG generation directly; tangential to end-to-end RAG robustness.

title: GraphSteal: Structural Knowledge Stealing from Graph RAG via Traversal Reconstruction
authors: Jinze Gu; Qinghua Mao; Xi Lin; Jun Wu
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box extraction attack against Graph RAG that reconstructs the underlying knowledge graph, exposing a privacy attack surface relevant to adversarial threats on RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy/structural extraction rather than poisoning, injection, or robustness of generation; narrower fit to the survey's adversarial-corruption theme.

title: FlashRT: Towards Computationally and Memory Efficient Red-Teaming for Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
authors: Yanting Wang; Chenlong Yin; Ying Chen; Jinyuan Jia
why_relevant: Proposes an efficient optimization-based red-teaming framework for prompt injection and knowledge corruption attacks against long-context LLMs, directly applicable to RAG security evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on efficiency of attack optimization rather than RAG-specific defenses or evaluation; relevance is mainly as a red-teaming tool.

title: Fast and Faithful: Real-Time Verification for Long-Document Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Xunzhuo Liu; Bowei He; Xue Liu; Haichen Zhang; Huamin Chen
why_relevant: Proposes a real-time faithfulness verifier for long-document RAG to detect unsupported/hallucinated responses, relevant to grounding verification and control mechanisms for unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on long-context verification engineering rather than directly on noise, conflict, or adversarial robustness.

title: Detecting RAG Extraction Attack via Dual-Path Runtime Integrity Game
authors: Yuanbo Xie; Yingjie Zhang; Yulin Li; Shouyou Song; Xiaokun Chen; Zhihan Liu; Liya Su; Tingwen Liu
why_relevant: Proposes a runtime defense (CanaryRAG) against RAG knowledge base extraction attacks, relevant to adversarial corruption/leakage threats in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy/extraction leakage rather than evidence corruption or generation robustness; tangential to core robustness themes.

title: Defenses Against Prompt Attacks Learn Surface Heuristics
authors: Shawn Li; Chenxiao Yu; Zhiyu Ni; Hao Li; Charith Peris; Chaowei Xiao; Yue Zhao
why_relevant: Analyzes failure modes of supervised fine-tuning defenses against prompt injection, including indirect injection via retrieved content relevant to RAG. Identifies shortcut biases (position, token trigger, topic) that cause over-rejection, informing defense design for RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on prompt-injection defenses generally rather than RAG-specific pipelines; RAG is one motivating application.

title: DRAINCODE: Stealthy Energy Consumption Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation via Context Poisoning
authors: Yanlin Wang; Jiadong Wu; Tianyue Jiang; Mingwei Liu; Jiachi Chen; Chong Wang; Ensheng Shi; Xilin Liu; Yuchi Ma; Zibin Zheng
why_relevant: Introduces a novel RAG context-poisoning attack targeting computational efficiency (energy/latency) in code generation, expanding the threat model for adversarial corruption of retrieval corpora.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to code generation and focuses on resource exhaustion rather than content correctness; tangential to mainstream RAG robustness concerns.

title: Context Shapes LLMs Retrieval-Augmented Fact-Checking Effectiveness
authors: Pietro Bernardelle; Stefano Civelli; Kevin Roitero; Gianluca Demartini
why_relevant: Analyzes how context length and evidence position affect LLM fact-checking accuracy, demonstrating lost-in-the-middle degradation and parametric vs evidence trade-offs relevant to distraction and knowledge conflict in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on fact-checking rather than general RAG; limited to positional/length analysis.

title: CoCR-RAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Web Q&A via Concept-oriented Context Reconstruction
authors: Kaize Shi; Xueyao Sun; Qika Lin; Firoj Alam; Qing Li; Xiaohui Tao; Guandong Xu
why_relevant: Proposes a context reconstruction method to filter noisy/redundant multi-source retrieved documents in RAG, addressing irrelevance and inconsistency in heterogeneous web evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on context compression/fusion rather than explicit robustness analysis, attacks, or calibration.

title: Asking For An Old Friend: Diagnosing and Mitigating Temporal Failure Modes in LLM-based Statutory Question Answering
authors: Max Prior; Andreas Schultz; Matthias Grabmair
why_relevant: Studies temporal knowledge conflict between parametric knowledge and retrieved evidence in legal QA, including recency bias and RAG-based mitigation with temporal filtering. Provides a benchmark for diagnosing failure modes relevant to context compliance and conflict resolution.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (German statutory law) and narrowly focused on temporal validity rather than broad RAG robustness.

title: Adaptive Retrieval helps Reasoning in LLMs -- but mostly if it's not used
authors: Srijan Shakya; Anamaria-Roberta Hartl; Sepp Hochreiter; Korbinian Pöppel
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Studies adaptive retrieval as a metacognitive decision of when to retrieve, showing static retrieval injects noise while the model's choice to forgo retrieval correlates with confidence/correctness. Directly relevant to calibration/control (when to retrieve) and uncertainty-aware RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Small-scale empirical study on math benchmarks with a single 8B model; limited methodological novelty.

title: Will It Still Be True Tomorrow? Multilingual Evergreen Question Classification to Improve Trustworthy QA
authors: Sergey Pletenev; Maria Marina; Nikolay Ivanov; Daria Galimzianova; Nikita Krayko; Mikhail Salnikov; Vasily Konovalov; Alexander Panchenko; Viktor Moskvoretskii
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Introduces evergreen/mutable question classification to inform when retrieval is needed, directly relevant to adaptive retrieval decisions and self-knowledge calibration in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on temporal classification rather than RAG robustness per se; RAG connection is via explaining GPT-4o retrieval behavior.

title: WeatherArchive-Bench: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Historical Weather Archives
authors: Yongan Yu; Xianda Du; Qingchen Hu; Jiahao Liang; Jingwei Ni; Dan Qiang; Kaiyu Huang; Grant McKenzie; Renee Sieber; Fengran Mo
why_relevant: Introduces a RAG benchmark over noisy OCR'd historical archives with archaic terminology, evaluating retrieval and reasoning robustness under unreliable, noisy evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (historical weather archives); focus is on benchmark construction rather than general robustness methods.

title: Unveiling Knowledge Utilization Mechanisms in LLM-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Yuhao Wang; Ruiyang Ren; Yucheng Wang; Wayne Xin Zhao; Jing Liu; Hua Wu; Haifeng Wang
why_relevant: Mechanistic analysis of how LLMs integrate parametric vs retrieved knowledge in RAG, with neuron-level interventions to shift reliance between sources — relevant to knowledge conflict and control.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is interpretability rather than robustness benchmarks or defenses; secondary relevance.

title: UR$^2$: Unify RAG and Reasoning through Reinforcement Learning
authors: Weitao Li; Boran Xiang; Xiaolong Wang; Zhinan Gou; Weizhi Ma; Yang Liu
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: when to retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes an RL framework that learns when to retrieve based on difficulty and uses LLM summarization to reduce noise, addressing retrieval-reasoning imbalance and robustness to noisy evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is unifying RAG with reasoning via RL; robustness/calibration aspects are secondary.

title: Towards a rigorous evaluation of RAG systems: the challenge of due diligence
authors: Grégoire Martinon; Alexandra Lorenzo de Brionne; Jérôme Bohard; Antoine Lojou; Damien Hervault; Nicolas J-B. Brunel
why_relevant: Proposes a rigorous hybrid human/LLM-judge evaluation protocol (inspired by PPI) for industrial RAG, quantifying hallucinations, off-topic, citation failures, and abstentions—relevant to evaluation of RAG reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (due diligence) and focused on evaluation methodology rather than robustness mechanisms; in French.

title: Support Evaluation for the TREC 2024 RAG Track: Comparing Human versus LLM Judges
authors: Nandan Thakur; Ronak Pradeep; Shivani Upadhyay; Daniel Campos; Nick Craswell; Jimmy Lin
why_relevant: Studies support/citation evaluation in RAG comparing LLM vs human judges, relevant to evaluation methodology for RAG faithfulness and reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on judge agreement rather than robustness under unreliable evidence per se.

title: Stealthy LLM-Driven Data Poisoning Attacks Against Embedding-Based Retrieval-Augmented Recommender Systems
authors: Fatemeh Nazary; Yashar Deldjoo; Tommaso Di Noia; Eugenio Di Sciascio
why_relevant: Studies stealthy data poisoning attacks on embedding-based RAG pipelines (in the recommender setting), relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval corpora.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to recommender systems rather than general QA RAG; narrower scope than canonical PoisonedRAG/BadRAG work.

title: Silent Leaks: Implicit Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems through Benign Queries
authors: Yuhao Wang; Wenjie Qu; Shengfang Zhai; Yanze Jiang; Zichen Liu; Yue Liu; Yinpeng Dong; Jiaheng Zhang
why_relevant: Introduces a stealthy knowledge extraction attack against RAG knowledge bases via benign queries, relevant to the adversarial threats subsection on RAG privacy/copyright leakage and defense evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on extraction/privacy rather than retrieval robustness or evidence reliability per se.

title: SAGE: A Framework of Precise Retrieval for RAG
authors: Jintao Zhang; Guoliang Li; Jinyang Su
why_relevant: SAGE addresses noisy and missing retrieval in RAG via semantic chunking, dynamic gradient-based chunk selection, and LLM self-feedback to adjust K, directly targeting noisy-context robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on retrieval precision/cost rather than adversarial robustness or calibration of abstention; relevance limited to noisy-retrieval subsection.

title: RECON: Reasoning with Condensation for Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhichao Xu; Minheng Wang; Yawei Wang; Wenqian Ye; Yuntao Du; Yunpu Ma; Yijun Tian
suggested_section: Noisy Retrieval / Context Filtering and Compression
why_relevant: RECON addresses noisy/verbose retrieved documents by introducing a learned summarizer that condenses evidence within an RL-based agentic RAG loop, mitigating context dilution and noise that degrade RAG performance.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is efficiency and accuracy via compression rather than robustness analysis, conflict, or adversarial settings.

title: RAGferee: Building Contextual Reward Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Andrei C. Coman; Ionut-Teodor Sorodoc; Leonardo F. R. Ribeiro; Bill Byrne; James Henderson; Adrià de Gispert
why_relevant: Trains contextual reward models that judge RAG responses on faithfulness, refusal when context is insufficient, and groundedness—relevant to calibration/abstention and evaluating RAG reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on reward modeling for RAG judging rather than directly defending against noisy/adversarial evidence.

title: RAGVUE: A Diagnostic View for Explainable and Automated Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Keerthana Murugaraj; Salima Lamsiyah; Martin Theobald
why_relevant: Proposes a diagnostic, reference-free RAG evaluation framework decomposing retrieval quality, grounding faithfulness, and judge calibration, relevant to evaluation metrics for unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on evaluation tooling rather than directly studying robustness to noise, conflict, or attacks.

title: RAG-targeted Adversarial Attack on LLM-based Threat Detection and Mitigation Framework
authors: Seif Ikbarieh; Kshitiz Aryal; Maanak Gupta
why_relevant: Demonstrates a word-level RAG knowledge-base poisoning attack on an LLM-based IoT threat-detection framework, relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Narrow IoT/NIDS application domain with small dataset; contribution is largely an applied case study using existing attack techniques (Textfooler, PoisonedRAG-style).

title: RAG in the Wild: On the (In)effectiveness of LLMs with Mixture-of-Knowledge Retrieval Augmentation
authors: Ran Xu; Yuchen Zhuang; Yue Yu; Haoyu Wang; Wenqi Shi; Carl Yang
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Empirically analyzes RAG effectiveness under realistic mixture-of-knowledge retrieval, showing rerankers add little, no source dominates, and LLMs fail to route queries—motivating adaptive retrieval and when-to-retrieve decisions.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on effectiveness analysis rather than directly tackling adversarial or conflict robustness.

title: PAIRS: Parametric-Verified Adaptive Information Retrieval and Selection for Efficient RAG
authors: Wang Chen; Guanqiang Qi; Weikang Li; Yang Li; Deguo Xia; Jizhou Huang
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: PAIRS adaptively decides when to retrieve by comparing parametric vs pseudo-context answers, and filters retrieved documents to mitigate irrelevant retrievals—directly relevant to adaptive retrieval control and noisy retrieval filtering.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on efficiency/accuracy rather than explicit robustness, calibration, or adversarial settings.

title: Optimizing What Matters: AUC-Driven Learning for Robust Neural Retrieval
authors: Nima Sheikholeslami; Erfan Hosseini; Patrice Bechard; Srivatsava Daruru; Sai Rajeswar
why_relevant: Proposes an AUC-aligned retriever training loss aimed at better global score calibration, enabling thresholding to filter irrelevant passages in RAG—relevant to calibration/control and noisy retrieval filtering.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on retriever training loss rather than end-to-end RAG robustness; calibration claims limited to retriever score separation.

title: On the Consistency of Multilingual Context Utilization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jirui Qi; Raquel Fernández; Arianna Bisazza
why_relevant: Studies how LLMs in multilingual RAG handle distracting passages across languages and consistency of context utilization, relevant to distraction and robustness evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is multilingual consistency rather than core robustness; distraction analysis is a secondary aspect.

title: MedTrust-RAG: Evidence Verification and Trust Alignment for Biomedical Question Answering
authors: Yingpeng Ning; Yuanyuan Sun; Ling Luo; Yanhua Wang; Yuchen Pan; Hongfei Lin
why_relevant: Proposes iterative retrieval-verification with citation-grounded reasoning and structured refusal (Negative Knowledge Assertions) to mitigate post-retrieval noise and hallucinations in biomedical RAG, addressing noisy evidence and abstention.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (biomedical) and primarily an applied method; not a general robustness study.

title: MTRAG: A Multi-Turn Conversational Benchmark for Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Yannis Katsis; Sara Rosenthal; Kshitij Fadnis; Chulaka Gunasekara; Young-Suk Lee; Lucian Popa; Vraj Shah; Huaiyu Zhu; Danish Contractor; Marina Danilevsky
why_relevant: MTRAG is a multi-turn RAG benchmark that explicitly tests unanswerable questions and non-standalone questions, evaluating how RAG systems handle these challenging cases relevant to abstention and uncertainty.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a general multi-turn RAG benchmark; robustness aspects (unanswerability) are one of several dimensions rather than the central focus.

title: LeakSealer: A Semisupervised Defense for LLMs Against Prompt Injection and Leakage Attacks
authors: Francesco Panebianco; Stefano Bonfanti; Francesco Trovò; Michele Carminati
why_relevant: Proposes a defense framework against prompt injection and PII leakage attacks targeting RAG systems, relevant to the adversarial corruption section.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is broader on LLM jailbreak/PII leakage detection rather than RAG-specific evidence robustness; RAG is only one of the scenarios.

title: LLM Embedding-based Attribution (LEA): Quantifying Source Contributions to Generative Model's Response for Vulnerability Analysis
authors: Reza Fayyazi; Michael Zuzak; Shanchieh Jay Yang
why_relevant: Proposes an attribution metric (LEA) that quantifies whether LLM outputs rely on retrieved context vs internal parametric knowledge, and evaluates behavior under valid, generic, and incorrect retrieval—directly relevant to knowledge conflict and auditing RAG reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to CVE/vulnerability analysis; method is more about attribution/auditing than improving robustness itself.

title: KnowGuard: Knowledge-Driven Abstention for Multi-Round Clinical Reasoning
authors: Xilin Dang; Kexin Chen; Xiaorui Su; Ayush Noori; Iñaki Arango; Lucas Vittor; Xinyi Long; Yuyang Du; Marinka Zitnik; Pheng Ann Heng
why_relevant: Proposes a knowledge-graph-grounded abstention method for multi-round clinical QA, addressing when LLMs should refrain from answering under insufficient evidence—directly relevant to abstention and calibration control under uncertainty.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (clinical) and focused on KG exploration rather than general RAG robustness; abstention is the main contribution.

title: Impact-driven Context Filtering For Cross-file Code Completion
authors: Yanzhou Li; Shangqing Liu; Kangjie Chen; Tianwei Zhang; Yang Liu
why_relevant: Proposes filtering of negative/irrelevant retrieved code chunks and adaptive on-demand retrieval, directly addressing noisy retrieval and retrieval control in code RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to repository-level code completion rather than general RAG robustness.

title: ICA-RAG: Information Completeness Guided Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Disease Diagnosis
authors: Jiawei He; Mingyi Jia; Zhihao Jia; Junwen Duan; Yan Song; Jianxin Wang
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes adaptive retrieval control deciding when to retrieve based on input information completeness, plus knowledge filtering to reduce noise—relevant to calibration/control and noisy retrieval mitigation in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (Chinese EMR clinical diagnosis); robustness is a side effect rather than the central focus.

title: Give LLMs a Security Course: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation via Knowledge Injection
authors: Bo Lin; Shangwen Wang; Yihao Qin; Liqian Chen; Xiaoguang Mao
why_relevant: Proposes a defense against knowledge base poisoning in retrieval-augmented code generation, directly addressing adversarial corruption in RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to code generation security rather than general RAG robustness.

title: FocusAgent: Simple Yet Effective Ways of Trimming the Large Context of Web Agents
authors: Imene Kerboua; Sahar Omidi Shayegan; Megh Thakkar; Xing Han Lù; Léo Boisvert; Massimo Caccia; Jérémy Espinas; Alexandre Aussem; Véronique Eglin; Alexandre Lacoste
why_relevant: FocusAgent uses LLM-based retrieval to prune noisy web observations and defend against indirect prompt injection attacks (banners, pop-ups), tackling both noisy context and adversarial corruption in a retrieval-augmented agent setting.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on web agents rather than general RAG over document corpora; relevance is via analogy to context filtering and injection defense.

title: Exploiting Web Search Tools of AI Agents for Data Exfiltration
authors: Dennis Rall; Bernhard Bauer; Mohit Mittal; Thomas Fraunholz
why_relevant: Empirically evaluates indirect prompt injection attacks against LLM agents using web-search/RAG tools for data exfiltration, relevant to the adversarial corruption section.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agent tool-calling security rather than RAG retrieval pipeline robustness specifically.

title: Efficient Context Selection for Long-Context QA: No Tuning, No Iteration, Just Adaptive-$k$
authors: Chihiro Taguchi; Seiji Maekawa; Nikita Bhutani
why_relevant: Proposes an adaptive method to dynamically decide how many passages to retrieve based on similarity score distributions, addressing the control problem of when/how much to retrieve and reducing noisy/irrelevant context.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on efficiency and accuracy rather than robustness per se; touches calibration-of-retrieval-size only indirectly.

title: ECoRAG: Evidentiality-guided Compression for Long Context RAG
authors: Yeonseok Jeong; Jinsu Kim; Dohyeon Lee; Seung-won Hwang
suggested_section: Distraction and Noisy Retrieval / Filtering and Compression
why_relevant: ECoRAG compresses retrieved documents based on evidentiality, explicitly filtering distractors and irrelevant content, and adaptively decides when more retrieval is needed—relevant to noisy retrieval, distraction, and retrieval control.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary framing is efficiency/compression for ODQA rather than robustness per se.

title: CoCoA: Collaborative Chain-of-Agents for Parametric-Retrieved Knowledge Synergy
authors: Yi Jiang; Sendong Zhao; Jianbo Li; Haochun Wang; Lizhe Zhang; Yan Liu; Bing Qin
why_relevant: Proposes a multi-agent framework that explicitly synergizes parametric and retrieved knowledge, addressing the parametric vs retrieved knowledge conflict and mitigating cases where retrieved content misleads generation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on performance improvement rather than systematic robustness analysis; conflict handling is implicit.

title: Bilevel Optimization for Covert Memory Tampering in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Architectures (XAMT)
authors: Akhil Sharma; Shaikh Yaser Arafat; Jai Kumar Sharma; Ken Huang
why_relevant: Proposes a bilevel optimization framework for covert poisoning of RAG knowledge bases (XAMT-RAG), evaluated on SafeRAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval memory.
why_not_or_caveat: Half the paper focuses on MARL replay buffers, not RAG; experimental section is largely protocol rather than results.

title: VERA: Validation and Enhancement for Retrieval Augmented systems
authors: Nitin Aravind Birur; Tanay Baswa; Divyanshu Kumar; Jatan Loya; Sahil Agarwal; Prashanth Harshangi
suggested_section: Calibration and Control (when to retrieve, filter, validate)
why_relevant: VERA proposes a control framework that decides whether retrieval is needed, filters irrelevant retrieved context, and validates response adherence/relevance, addressing noisy retrieval and calibration/control concerns in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Prompt-based pipeline with limited novelty; does not address adversarial or conflict settings.

title: Superposition Prompting: Improving and Accelerating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Thomas Merth; Qichen Fu; Mohammad Rastegari; Mahyar Najibi
why_relevant: Proposes a prompting method that prunes irrelevant retrieved documents to mitigate the distraction phenomenon in RAG, directly addressing robustness to noisy/irrelevant context.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary motivation is also efficiency; robustness is a secondary benefit.

title: Rationale-Guided Retrieval Augmented Generation for Medical Question Answering
authors: Jiwoong Sohn; Yein Park; Chanwoong Yoon; Sihyeon Park; Hyeon Hwang; Mujeen Sung; Hyunjae Kim; Jaewoo Kang
why_relevant: Proposes a rationale-guided filtering method using perplexity-based labels to filter distractor snippets and mitigate retriever bias in medical RAG, addressing noisy retrieval and selective augmentation.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to biomedical QA; not a general robustness study.

title: Provenance: A Light-weight Fact-checker for Retrieval Augmented LLM Generation Output
authors: Hithesh Sankararaman; Mohammed Nasheed Yasin; Tanner Sorensen; Alessandro Di Bari; Andreas Stolcke
why_relevant: Proposes a lightweight NLI-based fact-checker for RAG outputs that detects unsupported claims and traces them to context chunks, relevant to post-hoc filtering/abstention and hallucination detection in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on output verification rather than directly addressing noisy retrieval, conflict, or adversarial robustness.

title: Permissive Information-Flow Analysis for Large Language Models
authors: Shoaib Ahmed Siddiqui; Radhika Gaonkar; Boris Köpf; David Krueger; Andrew Paverd; Ahmed Salem; Shruti Tople; Lukas Wutschitz; Menglin Xia; Santiago Zanella-Béguelin
why_relevant: Proposes an information-flow label propagation defense for RAG/LLM-agent settings where retrieved documents may be poisoned or untrusted, addressing integrity/confidentiality robustness in retrieval pipelines.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on system-level taint tracking rather than core RAG robustness methods; tangential to noise/conflict/calibration themes.

title: LLM Robustness Against Misinformation in Biomedical Question Answering
authors: Alexander Bondarenko; Adrian Viehweger
why_relevant: Evaluates LLM robustness in RAG against prompt-injection of misinformation in the biomedical domain, using ASR and accuracy drop metrics across multiple models.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (biomedical) and limited methodological novelty; focuses only on augmented generation, not retrieval.

title: Granite Guardian
authors: Inkit Padhi; Manish Nagireddy; Giandomenico Cornacchia; Subhajit Chaudhury; Tejaswini Pedapati; Pierre Dognin; Keerthiram Murugesan; Erik Miehling; Martín Santillán Cooper; Kieran Fraser; Giulio Zizzo; Muhammad Zaid Hameed; Mark Purcell; Michael Desmond; Qian Pan; Zahra Ashktorab; Inge Vejsbjerg; Elizabeth M. Daly; Michael Hind; Werner Geyer; Ambrish Rawat; Kush R. Varshney; Prasanna Sattigeri
suggested_section: Calibration and control / guardrails for RAG
why_relevant: Granite Guardian provides RAG-specific risk detection including context relevance, groundedness, and answer relevance, which directly relates to filtering unreliable evidence and detecting hallucinations in RAG pipelines.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a general-purpose safety guardrail model; RAG robustness is one of several capabilities rather than the central focus.

title: GRAMMAR: Grounded and Modular Methodology for Assessment of Closed-Domain Retrieval-Augmented Language Model
authors: Xinzhe Li; Ming Liu; Shang Gao
why_relevant: Proposes a modular evaluation framework for closed-domain RAG that diagnoses whether failures stem from retrieval or LM, including robustness to query form variations. Relevant to evaluation methodology for unreliable RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on closed-domain evaluation and diagnostic protocol rather than directly studying noise, conflict, or adversarial attacks.

title: Flooding Spread of Manipulated Knowledge in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Communities
authors: Tianjie Ju; Yiting Wang; Xinbei Ma; Pengzhou Cheng; Haodong Zhao; Yulong Wang; Lifeng Liu; Jian Xie; Zhuosheng Zhang; Gongshen Liu
why_relevant: Demonstrates how manipulated knowledge can persist and spread via RAG when benign agents store and retrieve poisoned chat histories, relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval corpora in multi-agent settings.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is on multi-agent knowledge spread rather than RAG robustness; RAG persistence is a secondary contribution.

title: Faux Polyglot: A Study on Information Disparity in Multilingual Large Language Models
authors: Nikhil Sharma; Kenton Murray; Ziang Xiao
why_relevant: Studies inter-context knowledge conflicts in multilingual RAG, showing language-based biases in retrieval and generation when conflicting evidence appears across languages.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on linguistic/cultural bias rather than core robustness mechanisms; uses synthetic fictional data.

title: Evaluating the Retrieval Component in LLM-Based Question Answering Systems
authors: Ashkan Alinejad; Krtin Kumar; Ali Vahdat
why_relevant: Proposes an LLM-based framework for evaluating retriever quality in RAG that accounts for LLMs' ability to ignore irrelevant contexts, addressing limitations of conventional IR metrics. Relevant to evaluation of retrieval reliability under noisy/imperfect retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on evaluation methodology rather than directly on robustness, conflict, or adversarial issues.

title: Context Quality Matters in Training Fusion-in-Decoder for Extractive Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Kosuke Akimoto; Kunihiro Takeoka; Masafumi Oyamada
suggested_section: Noisy retrieval and training under irrelevant passages
why_relevant: Analyzes how context quality (proportion of relevant vs irrelevant passages) during FiD training affects robustness at inference, and proposes a cross-attention bias method to mitigate overfitting to specific context quality.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on FiD-specific training dynamics rather than general LLM RAG robustness.

title: Compressing Long Context for Enhancing RAG with AMR-based Concept Distillation
authors: Kaize Shi; Xueyao Sun; Qing Li; Guandong Xu
why_relevant: Proposes AMR-based concept distillation to compress retrieved documents and filter noisy/irrelevant content, addressing distraction from noisy retrieval in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on context compression rather than explicit robustness evaluation under adversarial or conflicting evidence.

title: BlendFilter: Advancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Query Generation Blending and Knowledge Filtering
authors: Haoyu Wang; Ruirui Li; Haoming Jiang; Jinjin Tian; Zhengyang Wang; Chen Luo; Xianfeng Tang; Monica Cheng; Tuo Zhao; Jing Gao
why_relevant: Proposes a knowledge filtering module to remove irrelevant retrieved passages and blends query augmentations to reduce noisy retrieval impact, relevant to the noisy retrieval and filtering subsection.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on QA performance improvement rather than systematic robustness analysis.

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
authors: Hanrong Zhang; Jingyuan Huang; Kai Mei; Yifei Yao; Zhenting Wang; Chenlu Zhan; Hongwei Wang; Yongfeng Zhang
why_relevant: ASB benchmarks attacks (including memory/RAG poisoning, indirect prompt injection, backdoors) and defenses on LLM agents, covering retrieval-stage adversarial corruption relevant to robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Scope is broader LLM-agent security, not purely RAG; only memory poisoning and IPI directly intersect with the survey.

title: A Troublemaker with Contagious Jailbreak Makes Chaos in Honest Towns
authors: Tianyi Men; Pengfei Cao; Zhuoran Jin; Yubo Chen; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Propagation in Agentic RAG
why_relevant: Proposes a retrieval-suffix-based poisoning/jailbreak attack on agent memory (RAG) that propagates across multi-agent systems, relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is multi-agent contagion rather than standard RAG robustness; tangential to core single-system RAG attacks.

title: A MapReduce Approach to Effectively Utilize Long Context Information in Retrieval Augmented Language Models
authors: Gongbo Zhang; Zihan Xu; Qiao Jin; Fangyi Chen; Yilu Fang; Yi Liu; Justin F. Rousseau; Ziyang Xu; Zhiyong Lu; Chunhua Weng; Yifan Peng
why_relevant: Proposes a map-reduce RAG framework to mitigate lost-in-the-middle and irrelevant context distraction, with analysis of conflicting context resolution and a preflight check to decide when extra processing is needed.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on medical QA application; not a central robustness study.

title: Tree of Clarifications: Answering Ambiguous Questions with Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Gangwoo Kim; Sungdong Kim; Byeongguk Jeon; Joonsuk Park; Jaewoo Kang
why_relevant: Addresses ambiguous queries in RAG by recursively generating disambiguated questions and pruning via self-verification, relevant to query ambiguity and control over clarification in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on long-form QA quality rather than robustness/calibration directly; ambiguity handling is the main connection.

title: [] Signature-Guided Adversarial Attacks On Healthcare LLMs: Exposing PII Leakage In RAG Systems
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption and attacks on RAG
why_relevant: Proposes a signature-guided adversarial prompting attack against RAG-based healthcare agents to extract PII, exposing privacy vulnerabilities in retrieval-augmented systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses narrowly on PII leakage in medical RAG rather than general robustness; domain-specific.

title: Towards Trustworthy Knowledge Graph Reasoning: An Uncertainty Aware Perspective
why_relevant: Applies conformal prediction and Learn-Then-Test to KG-based RAG for uncertainty quantification with coverage guarantees, relevant to calibration/uncertainty in retrieval-augmented reasoning.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on KG-RAG rather than text-passage RAG; does not address noise, conflict, or adversarial settings.

title: RAG-Thief: Scalable Extraction of Private Data from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Applications with Agent-based Attacks
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box agent-based attack to extract verbatim knowledge base content from RAG applications, relevant to privacy/IP attacks on RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on data extraction/IP leakage rather than evidence corruption or robustness per se; tangential to the core robustness taxonomy.

title: RAG-QA Arena: Evaluating Domain Robustness for Long-form Retrieval Augmented Question Answering
why_relevant: Introduces LFRQA and RAG-QA Arena for evaluating cross-domain (OOD) robustness of long-form RAG-QA systems across seven domains, relevant to evaluation under distribution shift.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on domain robustness and long-form answer evaluation rather than noise, conflict, or adversarial robustness.

title: Poison-RAG: Adversarial Data Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Recommender Systems
why_relevant: Proposes a data poisoning attack on RAG-based recommender systems by manipulating item metadata, relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval corpora.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to recommender systems rather than general QA RAG; narrow scope.

title: SIGHT: Reinforcement Learning with Self-Evidence and Information-Gain Diverse Branching for Search Agent
authors: Wenlin Zhong; Jinluan Yang; Yiquan Wu; Yi Liu; Jianhang Yao; Kun Kuang
why_relevant: SIGHT explicitly addresses noisy retrieval in multi-turn search agents, proposing information-gain-driven branching and self-evidence distillation to mitigate 'Tunnel Vision' from low SNR retrievals.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on RL search agent exploration rather than core RAG robustness; relevance is tangential to noise handling.

title: Memory Poisoning Attack and Defense on Memory Based LLM-Agents
authors: Balachandra Devarangadi Sunil; Isheeta Sinha; Piyush Maheshwari; Shantanu Todmal; Shreyan Mallik; Shuchi Mishra
why_relevant: Studies memory poisoning attacks (MINJA) on memory/RAG-augmented LLM agents and proposes trust-scoring and memory sanitization defenses with calibration analysis, relevant to adversarial corruption and defense calibration in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on agent memory rather than standard retrieval corpora; narrow EHR domain case study.

title: Detecting AI Hallucinations in Finance: An Information-Theoretic Method Cuts Hallucination Rate by 92%
authors: Mainak Singha
why_relevant: Proposes a hallucination detection method for RAG that combines semantic entropy with an evidence-capacity measure via perplexity decomposition, targeting cases where models ignore or conflict with retrieved evidence. Relevant to calibration/abstention and detecting unsupported answers.
why_not_or_caveat: Small (n=200) synthetic financial QA evaluation; limited validation and narrow domain.

title: Fighting Numerical Hallucinations via Data-centric Compilation for Online Financial QA
authors: Hao Chen; Xing Tang; Qirui Liu; Weijie Shi; Shiwei Li; Fuyuan Lyu; Weihong Luo; Xiku Du; Xiuqiang He
why_relevant: Proposes a data-centric RAG framework targeting noise sensitivity and hallucination in financial numerical QA via adversarial noise injection and verifiable program synthesis, directly addressing robustness to noisy/conflicting retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (financial numerical QA); robustness contributions are application-tied rather than general.

title: VerifAI: A Verifiable Open-Source Search Engine for Biomedical Question Answering
authors: Miloš Košprdić; Adela Ljajić; Bojana Bašaragin; Darija Medvecki; Lorenzo Cassano; Nikola Milošević
why_relevant: VerifAI integrates post-hoc NLI-based claim verification into a biomedical RAG pipeline to detect hallucinations and reduce unsupported citations, relevant to verification/control mechanisms for unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific application rather than general robustness study; verification is a known technique applied to biomedical QA.

title: Towards Order Fairness: Mitigating LLMs Order Sensitivity through Dual Group Advantage Optimization
authors: Xu Chu; Guanyu Wang; Zhijie Tan; Xinrong Chen; Ziyu Li; Tong Mo; Weiping Li
suggested_section: Distraction and positional sensitivity in RAG
why_relevant: Addresses LLM order sensitivity in RAG contexts, proposes an RL method (DGAO) to improve robustness to passage ordering, and introduces Consistency/Overconfidence metrics relevant to evaluating RAG robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Order bias is only one facet of unreliable evidence; not centrally about noisy/conflicting/adversarial retrieval.

title: To Retrieve or To Think? An Agentic Approach for Context Evolution
authors: Rubing Chen; Jian Wang; Wenjie Li; Xiao-Yong Wei; Qing Li
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes an adaptive retrieve-or-think agent framework that decides when to retrieve vs. reason internally, directly addressing over-retrieval noise and control of retrieval—relevant to calibration/control of when to retrieve.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on multi-hop QA efficiency/accuracy rather than explicit robustness analysis; limited evaluation depth.

title: Tiny-Critic RAG: Empowering Agentic Fallback with Parameter-Efficient Small Language Models
authors: Yichao Wu; Penghao Liang; Yafei Xiang; Mengwei Yuan; Jianan Liu; Jing Yang; Xianyou Li; Weiran Yan
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: gatekeeping and fallback routing
why_relevant: Proposes a small LM critic for routing/fallback decisions in RAG under noisy/adversarial retrieval, addressing when to trust retrieved evidence vs. re-retrieve — relevant to calibration/control and noisy retrieval handling.
why_not_or_caveat: Limited evaluation (5k queries, two datasets), and arxiv ID seems suspicious; mostly an engineering/efficiency contribution rather than deep robustness analysis.

title: The Override Gap: A Magnitude Account of Knowledge Conflict Failure in Hypernetwork-Based Instant LLM Adaptation
authors: Shuaizhi Cheng; Xiang Shi; Zhiwei Zhang; Mingwei Li
why_relevant: Studies knowledge conflict between parametric pretrained knowledge and new document-derived knowledge injected via hypernetwork adapters, proposes conflict-aware mechanisms, and releases a benchmark grading conflicts by prior strength. Comparisons to RAG on conflict tiers are directly relevant.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on parameter-space internalization rather than retrieval-augmented generation per se; relevance is via the conflict framing and benchmark.

title: Structure-Aware RAG: Structured Retrieval Augmented Generation from Noisy Data for Conversational Agents
authors: Kaiqiao Han; LuAn Tang; Renliang Sun; Peng Yuan; Wei Cheng; Haoyu Wang; Wei Wang; Yizhou Sun; Haifeng Chen
why_relevant: Proposes a structured (table-based) RAG framework explicitly designed to handle noisy conversational data, addressing noisy/irrelevant retrieval contexts.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on method design for conversational agents rather than systematic robustness analysis; relevance to broader noise/conflict taxonomy is limited.

title: Self-Correcting RAG: Enhancing Faithfulness via MMKP Context Selection and NLI-Guided MCTS
authors: Shijia Xu; Zhou Wu; Xiaolong Jia; Yu Wang; Kai Liu; April Xiaowen Dong
why_relevant: Proposes context selection as MMKP to remove redundancy and NLI-guided MCTS to verify faithfulness, addressing hallucination and low context utilization in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on multi-hop reasoning quality rather than explicit robustness to noisy/adversarial evidence; relevance is moderate.

title: SEAL-Tag: Self-Tag Evidence Aggregation with Probabilistic Circuits for PII-Safe Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jin Xie; Songze Li; Guang Cheng
why_relevant: Proposes a defense against contextual PII leakage and adaptive extraction attacks in RAG, including a benchmark for leakage evaluation, relevant to the adversarial corruption subsection.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy leakage rather than general robustness/noise/conflict; narrower scope on PII protection.

title: SE-Search: Self-Evolving Search Agent via Memory and Dense Reward
authors: Jian Li; Yizhang Jin; Dongqi Liu; Hang Ding; Jiafu Wu; Dongsheng Chen; Yunhang Shen; Yulei Qin; Ying Tai; Chengjie Wang; Xiaotong Yuan; Yabiao Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a search agent that filters noisy retrieved documents via memory purification and uses dense rewards to control when/what to search, addressing noisy retrieval and retrieval control.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on agent training rather than systematic robustness analysis; does not address conflict, adversarial, or calibration of uncertainty.

title: SD-RAG: A Prompt-Injection-Resilient Framework for Selective Disclosure in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Aiman Al Masoud; Marco Arazzi; Antonino Nocera
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption and prompt injection defenses
why_relevant: Proposes a defense against prompt injection in RAG by enforcing privacy/disclosure constraints at retrieval time, relevant to adversarial corruption and policy-aware control.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on selective disclosure/privacy rather than general robustness to noisy or conflicting evidence.

title: S2G-RAG: Structured Sufficiency and Gap Judging for Iterative Retrieval-Augmented QA
authors: Minghan Li; Junjie Zou; Xinxuan Lv; Chao Zhang; Guodong Zhou
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve and Stop
why_relevant: Proposes an iterative RAG controller that judges evidence sufficiency and structured information gaps, deciding when to stop or re-retrieve, and mitigates distractor/noise accumulation via sentence-level evidence extraction.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on multi-hop QA control rather than explicit adversarial or conflict robustness; suspicious arXiv ID (2604.xxxxx) suggests possibly unverified preprint.

title: Retrieval Pivot Attacks in Hybrid RAG: Measuring and Mitigating Amplified Leakage from Vector Seeds to Graph Expansion
authors: Scott Thornton
why_relevant: Introduces a new attack surface (retrieval pivot attacks) in hybrid vector+graph RAG, with metrics for leakage and defenses, fitting the adversarial corruption and security aspects of robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on cross-tenant data leakage/access control rather than core robustness to noisy/conflicting evidence; somewhat niche to hybrid GraphRAG.

title: RepoShapley: Shapley-Enhanced Context Filtering for Repository-Level Code Completion
authors: Yu Huo; Kun Zeng; Siyu Zhang; Yuquan Lu; Cheng Yang; Yifu Guo; Xiaoying Tang
why_relevant: Proposes coalition-aware context filtering using Shapley values to remove harmful/conflicting retrieved chunks and control when to retrieve, directly addressing noisy retrieval and retrieval control in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (repository-level code completion); robustness framing is secondary to code completion utility.

title: Relink: Constructing Query-Driven Evidence Graph On-the-Fly for GraphRAG
authors: Manzong Huang; Chenyang Bu; Yi He; Xingrui Zhuo; Xindong Wu
suggested_section: Distraction and Noisy Retrieval in GraphRAG
why_relevant: Relink targets distractor facts and missing evidence in GraphRAG by dynamically constructing query-specific evidence graphs, directly addressing noisy retrieval and distraction in graph-based RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on GraphRAG performance gains rather than systematic robustness evaluation; conflict/adversarial aspects not addressed.

title: RUBEN: Rule-Based Explanations for Retrieval-Augmented LLM Systems
authors: Joel Rorseth; Parke Godfrey; Lukasz Golab; Divesh Srivastava; Jarek Szlichta
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: analysis and explanation tools
why_relevant: RUBEN mines rule-based explanations that identify which RAG sources cause unsafe outputs, applied to testing adversarial prompt injection and data poisoning resilience in RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily an explainability/demo tool rather than a robustness method or benchmark; coverage of attacks/defenses is illustrative.

title: PlanGuard: Defending Agents against Indirect Prompt Injection via Planning-based Consistency Verification
authors: Guangyu Gong; Zizhuang Deng
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Prompt Injection Defenses
why_relevant: Proposes a defense against indirect prompt injection in LLM agents using retrieved content, relevant to adversarial corruption of external/retrieved context.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on agent tool-use rather than RAG QA; IPI defense via plan consistency is tangential to retrieval pipeline robustness.

title: Parametric Knowledge and Retrieval Behavior in RAG Fine-Tuning for Electronic Design Automation
authors: Julian Oestreich; Maximilian Bley; Frank Binder; Lydia Müller; Maksym Sydorenko; André Alcalde
suggested_section: Evaluation and metrics for RAG under noisy retrieval
why_relevant: Studies RAG fine-tuning robustness under varying retrieval conditions (relevant, irrelevant, noisy, missing) and proposes a triple-based evaluation metric (PKP) that disentangles parametric vs retrieved knowledge, relevant to evaluation and knowledge conflict.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (EDA) and focuses on a custom metric rather than general robustness methods.

title: Panini: Continual Learning in Token Space via Structured Memory
authors: Shreyas Rajesh; Pavan Holur; Mehmet Yigit Turali; Chenda Duan; Vwani Roychowdhury
suggested_section: Calibration and Abstention / Structured memory alternatives to chunk RAG
why_relevant: Panini explicitly targets reliability issues in RAG: it reduces unsupported/hallucinated generation from irrelevant chunk context and evaluates abstention on unanswerable queries via curated splits.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a structured-memory/efficiency method; robustness/abstention is a secondary contribution rather than the central focus.

title: Ontology-Guided Neuro-Symbolic Inference: Grounding Language Models with Mathematical Domain Knowledge
authors: Marcelo Labre
why_relevant: The paper empirically shows that retrieval quality determines whether RAG helps or hurts: high-relevance ontology context improves accuracy while irrelevant retrieved definitions actively degrade performance, directly illustrating distraction and noisy retrieval effects.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (mathematics with OpenMath ontology) rather than a general robustness study; contribution to robustness is incidental.

title: Mitigating Hallucination in Financial Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Fine-Grained Knowledge Verification
authors: Taoye Yin; Haoyuan Hu; Yaxin Fan; Xinhao Chen; Xinya Wu; Kai Deng; Kezun Zhang; Feng Wang
why_relevant: Addresses hallucinations in RAG where generated answers conflict with retrieved evidence, using fine-grained faithfulness rewards via RL to improve context compliance.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (financial) and a fairly narrow methodological contribution; not a central robustness paper.

title: MASS-RAG: Multi-Agent Synthesis Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Xingchen Xiao; Heyan Huang; Runheng Liu; Jincheng Xie
suggested_section: Noisy Retrieval: Filtering and Multi-Agent Defenses
why_relevant: Proposes a multi-agent filtering and synthesis framework specifically aimed at handling noisy, incomplete, and heterogeneous retrieved contexts in RAG, directly relevant to noisy retrieval robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Method paper focused on accuracy improvements rather than systematic robustness analysis; suspicious arXiv ID (2604) suggests possible metadata issue.

title: Learning When to Remember: Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandits for Abstention-Aware Memory Retrieval in LLM-Based Coding Agents
authors: Mehmet Iscan
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: when to retrieve and abstain
why_relevant: Proposes a risk-sensitive contextual bandit controller that decides whether to inject retrieved memory, abstain, ask for feedback, or skip retrieval, with explicit false-positive penalties. Directly addresses when-to-retrieve/trust and abstention in an agentic RAG-like memory setting.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain is narrow (coding-agent issue memory) and evaluation is small-scale, deterministic proxy rather than full RAG benchmarks.

title: LIT-RAGBench: Benchmarking Generator Capabilities of Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Koki Itai; Shunichi Hasegawa; Yuta Yamamoto; Gouki Minegishi; Masaki Otsuki
why_relevant: Introduces a generator benchmark covering abstention when evidence is missing, alongside integration, reasoning, logic, and table understanding—relevant for evaluation of RAG robustness and abstention behavior.
why_not_or_caveat: Small Japanese-origin dataset (114 questions); focuses on generator capabilities broadly rather than centrally on noise/conflict/adversarial robustness.

title: From Conflict to Consensus: Boosting Medical Reasoning via Multi-Round Agentic RAG
authors: Wenhao Wu; Zhentao Tang; Yafu Li; Shixiong Kai; Mingxuan Yuan; Chunlin Chen; Zhi Wang
suggested_section: Calibration and control: when to retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes adaptive multi-round RAG that uses semantic conflict among candidate answers as a signal to trigger retrieval, addressing noisy token-level uncertainty and long-context degradation. Relevant to adaptive retrieval control and conflict-based refinement.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (medical QA); robustness framing is secondary to test-time scaling for reasoning.

title: Finding What Matters: Anchoring Context Knowledge with Evolving Indices for Iterative Retrieval
authors: Mingyan Wu; Zhenghao Liu; Xinze Li; Yuqing Lan; Yukun Yan; Shuo Wang; Cheng Yang; Minghe Yu; Zheni Zeng; Maosong Sun
why_relevant: Proposes an iterative RAG method that anchors key evidence to mitigate noise accumulation across retrieval steps in multi-hop QA, addressing context noise and lost-in-the-middle issues.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a multi-hop QA performance method; robustness to noise is a motivation but not rigorously benchmarked under adversarial or strongly unreliable evidence.

title: FAITH: Factuality Alignment through Integrating Trustworthiness and Honestness
authors: Xiaoning Dong; Chengyan Wu; Yajie Wen; Yu Chen; Yun Xue; Jing Zhang; Wei Xu; Bolei Ma
why_relevant: FAITH is a post-training method for factuality alignment that integrates uncertainty estimation (consistency, semantic entropy) with a RAG module to rectify low-confidence responses, relevant to calibration/control and knowing when to trust internal vs external knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on factuality alignment via uncertainty-aware RL; RAG is auxiliary rather than the core robustness contribution.

title: FACTUM: Mechanistic Detection of Citation Hallucination in Long-Form RAG
authors: Maxime Dassen; Rebecca Kotula; Kenton Murray; Andrew Yates; Dawn Lawrie; Efsun Kayi; James Mayfield; Kevin Duh
why_relevant: Proposes a mechanistic detector for citation hallucination in long-form RAG by decoupling attention (context) vs FFN (parametric) pathways, directly relevant to parametric-vs-retrieved conflict and reliability/calibration of RAG outputs.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused narrowly on citation attribution hallucination detection via interpretability, not broader robustness; somewhat tangential to noise/attack/OOD topics.

title: Enhancing Legal LLMs through Metadata-Enriched RAG Pipelines and Direct Preference Optimization
authors: Suyash Maniyar; Deepali Singh; Rohith Reddy
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: Abstention under insufficient context
why_relevant: Proposes DPO training to enforce safe refusal when retrieved context is insufficient, and improves retrieval to reduce errors in legal RAG—directly addressing abstention/control and noisy retrieval failure modes.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (legal) application; contribution is incremental and narrow.

title: Context-Length Robustness in Question Answering Models: A Comparative Empirical Study
authors: Trishita Dhara; Siddhesh Sheth
why_relevant: Empirically studies how injecting irrelevant context degrades QA accuracy while preserving the answer-bearing evidence, directly relevant to distraction and context dilution in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Limited novelty; small-scale empirical study on SQuAD/HotpotQA, not specifically about retrieval pipelines.

title: Claim-Selective Certification for High-Risk Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Shao Kan
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: Abstention and Conflict Handling
why_relevant: Proposes a claim-level certification and abstain/partial/conflict action policy for medical RAG under mixed evidence, addressing knowledge conflict, selective abstention, and calibration of action decisions with dedicated metrics (UCCR, PAU).
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (medical) and uses weak-label protocol with limited generality; relies on template decomposition and cue-based scoring.

title: Cited but Not Verified: Parsing and Evaluating Source Attribution in LLM Deep Research Agents
authors: Hailey Onweller; Elias Lumer; Austin Huber; Pia Ramchandani; Vamse Kumar Subbiah; Corey Feld
why_relevant: Introduces an evaluation framework for citation reliability in deep research RAG agents, measuring link validity, relevance, and factual accuracy, and shows factual accuracy degrades as retrieval depth scales—relevant to evaluation of unreliable evidence and citation trustworthiness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on citation/attribution evaluation rather than robustness mechanisms; tangential to noise/conflict/adversarial axes.

title: Adversarial Yet Cooperative: Multi-Perspective Reasoning in Retrieved-Augmented Language Models
authors: Can Xu; Lingyong Yan; Jiayi Wu; Haosen Wang; Shuaiqiang Wang; Yuchen Li; Jizhou Huang; Dawei Yin; Xiang Li
why_relevant: Proposes a reasoner-verifier multi-agent RAG framework with uncertainty/entropy-based process rewards to handle partial, conflicting, or misleading retrieved documents, relevant to calibration/control and conflict handling.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is RL reward design for agentic RAG rather than systematic robustness study; robustness to unreliable evidence is motivational rather than the main contribution.

title: ADAM: A Systematic Data Extraction Attack on Agent Memory via Adaptive Querying
authors: Xingyu Lyu; Jianfeng He; Ning Wang; Yidan Hu; Tao Li; Danjue Chen; Shixiong Li; Yimin Chen
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG
why_relevant: Proposes a privacy/data-extraction attack against RAG-style memory in LLM agents, relevant to adversarial robustness of retrieval-augmented systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy leakage from agent memory rather than evidence reliability or generation robustness; tangential to core RAG robustness themes.

title: Train for Truth, Keep the Skills: Binary Retrieval-Augmented Reward Mitigates Hallucinations
authors: Tong Chen; Akari Asai; Luke Zettlemoyer; Hannaneh Hajishirzi; Faeze Brahman
why_relevant: Proposes RL with binary retrieval-augmented reward to reduce hallucinations and induce calibrated abstention (IDK), directly relevant to calibration/control and abstention behavior in RAG-related factuality training.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on post-training factuality rather than RAG inference robustness; retrieval is used for reward verification, not as the system's evidence pipeline.

title: Towards Agents That Know When They Don't Know: Uncertainty as a Control Signal for Structured Reasoning
authors: Josefa Lia Stoisser; Marc Boubnovski Martell; Lawrence Phillips; Gianluca Mazzoni; Lea Mørch Harder; Philip Torr; Jesper Ferkinghoff-Borg; Kaspar Martens; Julien Fauqueur
suggested_section: Calibration and Control (abstention and uncertainty-guided retrieval)
why_relevant: Proposes using retrieval uncertainty (entropy over table-selection rollouts) and summary uncertainty as control signals for abstention, filtering, and RL training in a structured-data agent, directly relevant to calibration/abstention in retrieval-augmented settings.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multi-table biomedical summarization rather than standard text RAG; relevance is via analogy of retrieval uncertainty and abstention control.

title: Towards Adaptive Memory-Based Optimization for Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Qitao Qin; Yucong Luo; Yihang Lu; Zhibo Chu; Xiaoman Liu; Xianwei Meng
why_relevant: Proposes adaptive RAG with memory, content filtering for noise reduction, and dynamic decisions on when to stop retrieval, touching on noisy retrieval and retrieval control.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on open-domain QA performance rather than explicitly studying robustness; relevance is incidental.

title: Tools in the Loop: Quantifying Uncertainty of LLM Question Answering Systems That Use Tools
authors: Panagiotis Lymperopoulos; Vasanth Sarathy
why_relevant: Proposes uncertainty quantification framework jointly modeling LLM and external tool/retriever uncertainty, with a RAG proof-of-concept on BoolQ. Relevant to calibration and uncertainty in RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: RAG is only a small proof-of-concept; primary focus is tool-calling broadly, not retrieval robustness.

title: Structured Relevance Assessment for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Aryan Raj; Astitva Veer Garg; Anitha D
suggested_section: Calibration and control: filtering and abstention
why_relevant: Proposes a relevance scoring + source reliability framework with abstention ('unknown' protocol) and balancing parametric vs retrieved knowledge, directly relevant to noisy retrieval handling and calibration/abstention in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Preliminary evaluation, limited rigor, and uses a non-standard benchmark; contribution is incremental.

title: SUCEA: Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval for Adversarial Fact-checking through Claim Decomposition and Editing
authors: Hongjun Liu; Yilun Zhao; Arman Cohan; Chen Zhao
why_relevant: Addresses adversarially crafted claims that break retrieval in RAG-based fact-checking, proposing claim decomposition and iterative editing to improve evidence retrieval under reasoning-intensive adversarial conditions.
why_not_or_caveat: Adversarial setting concerns adversarial claims rather than corpus poisoning or prompt injection; narrower fact-checking scope.

title: Proof-Carrying Numbers (PCN): A Protocol for Trustworthy Numeric Answers from LLMs via Claim Verification
authors: Aivin V. Solatorio
suggested_section: Calibration and control: verification and abstention
why_relevant: Proposes a presentation-layer verification protocol for numeric outputs in RAG-style systems, addressing fidelity, hallucination, and fail-closed abstention behavior—relevant to calibration/control and trust under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses narrowly on numeric span verification at the renderer, not on retrieval noise, conflict, or attacks directly.

title: PluriHopRAG: Exhaustive, Recall-Sensitive QA Through Corpus-Specific Document Structure Learning
authors: Mykolas Sveistrys; Richard Kunert
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark and method explicitly targeting distractor-heavy, recall-sensitive retrieval over repetitive corpora, directly addressing distraction and noisy retrieval challenges in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on exhaustive aggregation QA rather than core robustness topics like conflict, attacks, or calibration.

title: MMKB-RAG: A Multi-Modal Knowledge-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework
authors: Zihan Ling; Zhiyao Guo; Yixuan Huang; Yi An; Shuai Xiao; Jinsong Lan; Xiaoyong Zhu; Bo Zheng
suggested_section: Calibration and control: when to retrieve and filter
why_relevant: Proposes a multi-modal RAG framework that decides when to retrieve, filters irrelevant documents, and reranks for consistency, addressing noisy retrieval and retrieval control in MLLMs.
